summary: Review-required audit trail for the live Windows Error Reporting cleanup card. The app already ships this file-backed cleanup action and the repo cleanup docs describe the same WER directories, but the card has not yet been promoted into the validated research-provider surface.

setting.name: Clear Windows Error Reporting Files
setting.casual_explanation: This deletes Windows Error Reporting crash dumps and report metadata from the tracked WER folders.
setting.why_people_change_it: People clear WER files when they want to reclaim disk space or remove queued crash-report artifacts after collecting what they need.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: Clearing WER files reclaims space, but it also removes pending crash-report artifacts and report metadata.
setting.professional_notes: The current app deletes WER content under %PROGRAMDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\WER, %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\WER, and %TEMP%\WER. Repo cleanup docs identify the same Windows Error Reporting cleanup surface.

allowed_values.label: No cleanup action
allowed_values.meaning: WER files remain until the operator or Windows removes them.

allowed_values.label: Clear WER files
allowed_values.meaning: Deletes the WER crash dumps and report metadata tracked by the current app.

decision.why: The live cleanup behavior and repo-backed file targets are clear, but this one-shot cleanup card still lives only in the first-party provider.
blocking_issues: The card has not yet been promoted from the first-party cleanup provider into the research-provider surface.
This is a maintenance action with no rollback support.
decision.promotion_disposition_reason: Closed as rejected for research-provider promotion because the live action is one-shot, destructive, high-risk, reboot-sensitive, or lacks a rollback story suitable for a validated tweak card.
decision.promotion_reopen_criteria: Reopen only if the app gains a verified rollback/snapshot contract and dedicated validation proof for the exact action.
